transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I’m probably making it sound bigger than it is, but I’ve been working on a memorial piece for my aunt, and I started getting these really upsetting thoughts that I might somehow dishonor her with it. Like if I put one photo in the wrong place, or chose the wrong color, it would mean I didn’t love her enough.

I know that sounds a little… dramatic, maybe. It just didn’t feel like normal creative doubt. I couldn’t really brush it off, and it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Have you been having these upsetting thoughts repeatedly, even when you try not to think about them?

Yes… I mean, I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but it wasn’t just a passing worry. When I was working on my aunt’s memorial piece, the same kind of awful thought kept coming back—like if I placed a photo wrong or picked the wrong color, it somehow meant I was dishonoring her or didn’t love her enough.

I tried to tell myself it was just creative doubt, but I couldn’t really brush it off the way I normally would.
Would you say these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt come into your mind against your will?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t sit down and decide to think that way. It just kind of barges in while I’m trying to work, like, “What if this choice means you’re dishonoring her?” or “What if that means you didn’t love her enough?”

I know it probably sounds excessive, and I don’t want to make it seem worse than it is, but it really did feel unwanted. I wanted to just treat it like normal creative uncertainty and move on, but I couldn’t quite brush it off.
Are these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt affecting your ability to do other things besides working on the memorial piece?

A little, yes… I mean, I’m still mostly functioning. I’m getting most of my work done, so I don’t want to make it sound like everything has fallen apart.

But the extra time I keep losing in the studio has started to matter. I missed a grant deadline because I couldn’t get things wrapped up, and I also backed out of a gallery talk that I actually had wanted to do. That felt… embarrassing to admit, honestly.
Are these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt keeping you up at night or making it hard for you to concentrate on things you normally enjoy?

Not so much keeping me up all night, I don’t think… or at least I wouldn’t want to say it that strongly. It’s more that when I’m in the studio, I lose so much extra time second-guessing things that it spills over.

I’m still getting most of my work done, mostly. But it already cost me a grant deadline, and I backed out of a gallery talk I’d actually been looking forward to, because I just couldn’t get things wrapped up. That’s probably the main way it’s affecting me.
Are these thoughts affecting your relationships with friends or family outside of your work?

I don’t think so… not in any obvious way, anyway. I mean, I haven’t had a big argument with anyone over it or anything like that.

Maybe I’ve been a little more distracted sometimes, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. If you mean, like, am I avoiding friends or upsetting my family because of it, I don’t think I’ve really noticed that.
Do these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt feel like they're a part of you, or do they feel foreign, like they're coming from outside of yourself?

They feel like they’re coming from me, I guess—not like a voice or anything outside of me. But they don’t feel like what I actually believe, if that makes sense.

It’s more like these awful, unwanted thoughts just kind of intrude when I’m working on my aunt’s memorial piece… like if I put one photo in the wrong place, or choose the wrong color, it somehow means I didn’t love her enough or I’m dishonoring her. And I know that sounds extreme. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. But I can’t just brush them off the way I would with normal creative doubts.
Are these thoughts affecting your daily routines or activities outside of work and relationships?

Outside of work and relationships… I think it’s mostly the work part, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like my whole life has fallen apart or anything.

I’m still getting most things done, but the extra time I lose in the studio has had consequences. I missed a grant deadline, and I ended up backing out of a gallery talk I’d actually wanted to do because I couldn’t get everything finished. So… daily routines, maybe not hugely, but activities connected to my art, yes.
Do you feel like you have to do something specific to make these upsetting thoughts about dishonoring your aunt go away?

Yes… I think I do, though I feel a little embarrassed saying it because it’s not like a formal ritual or anything.

I’ll reread the label text, or move the same objects on the table just slightly, and then check the layout photos again and again until it feels… settled, I guess. Part of me knows it’s probably already fine, and I’m just losing studio time, but in the moment it feels hard to stop before I get that feeling.
Do you feel like doing these specific things, like rereading the label text or rearranging objects, is necessary to prevent something bad from happening?

I don’t think I believe something bad will literally happen, exactly. It’s more like… if I don’t reread the label text or nudge things into place and check the layout photos again, I’m left with this awful feeling that it’s not right, like I’ve been careless with her memory.

I know part of me can see it’s probably already fine. I really do. But I still keep doing it until it feels settled enough to stop, if that makes sense. I’m aware it costs me studio time, so I’m not trying to make it sound reasonable.
Do you feel like rereading the label text or rearranging objects helps to reduce your anxiety about dishonoring your aunt?

Yes… I mean, in the moment it does help, or it feels like it helps. I’ll reread the label text, nudge the objects a little, check the layout photos again, and the anxiety kind of drops once it feels “settled.”

I know that probably sounds a bit unnecessary, and part of me does know it’s already fine. I’m not trying to be difficult or make extra work for myself. It’s just that if I stop before I get that feeling, I stay really uneasy, like I haven’t done right by her.
Do you think that if you didn't do these things, like rereading the label text or rearranging objects, something specifically bad would happen to you or your aunt's memory?

Not specifically, no… I don’t think I believe there’s a clear consequence, like something terrible will happen to me or that her memory will actually be harmed.

It’s more that I get this really uncomfortable feeling that it’s not settled or respectful enough, and then I’ll end up rereading the label text, nudging the same objects on the table, checking the layout photos over and over. I know part of me can see it’s already fine, and I’m just losing studio time, but stopping before it feels right is… hard. Does that make sense?

Do you think the uncomfortable feeling you get if you don't reread the label text or rearrange objects is because you're afraid of something specific going wrong, or is it more about just feeling anxious or uneasy in general?

It’s… more than just general anxiety, I think. I don’t want to overstate it, because I know it’s not logical exactly, but there are these unwanted thoughts that if I choose the wrong photo placement or the wrong color, it somehow means I’m dishonoring my aunt, or that I didn’t love her enough.

I know that sounds harsh when I say it out loud. It’s not like I truly believe one object being slightly off proves that, but the thought hits me that way, and then I feel like I have to fix it or check it until I can calm down. Does that answer what you mean?
Is the reason you reread the label text or rearrange objects because you believe it will prevent something bad from happening to your aunt's memory, or is it just to make yourself feel less anxious?

I think it’s more to make myself feel less anxious… or to get that “settled” feeling. I don’t really believe I’m preventing some concrete bad thing from happening to her memory.

It’s just that if I don’t do it, I keep feeling like something is off. So I’ll end up rereading the label text, nudging the same objects on the table, and checking the layout photos over and over until it feels okay enough to stop. I know part of me knows it’s already fine, and honestly I’m just losing studio time, but it’s hard to leave it alone before it feels right.
Do you think the reason you're doing these repetitive checks is because you're afraid of making a mistake itself, or because you're afraid of what might happen as a result of that mistake?

I think it’s less that I’m afraid of a practical mistake, like the piece will look wrong, and more what the mistake would… mean, I guess.

Like when I was working on my aunt’s memorial piece, I’d get these awful thoughts that if I chose the wrong photo placement or the wrong color, it meant I was dishonoring her somehow, or that I didn’t love her enough. I know that sounds kind of extreme, and I don’t want it to come across like I fully believe that, but I couldn’t just brush it off like normal creative doubt. It felt really upsetting, so I kept checking. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you need to get everything exactly right when working on your aunt's memorial piece?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I know with art there’s always some amount of wanting it to be right, especially because it was for my aunt, but this felt more intense than normal.

It was like if one photo placement or color choice was wrong, this awful thought would pop up that I was dishonoring her, or that it meant I didn’t love her enough. I know that sounds a bit dramatic, and I’m not saying it makes sense, but I couldn’t really brush it off the way I usually would with regular creative doubt.
Is your need to get everything exactly right when working on your aunt's memorial piece because you're afraid of the mistake itself or what it might mean about your feelings for her?

It’s more about what it would mean, I think. Not the mistake in itself, exactly.

Like, I know a photo being a little off or a color not being perfect isn’t some terrible thing on its own. But with my aunt’s memorial piece, I kept having these really awful, unwanted thoughts that if I chose wrong, it meant I was dishonoring her somehow… or that I didn’t love her enough. I feel embarrassed saying that, because I do know it doesn’t sound fully rational. But I couldn’t just brush it off like normal creative doubt.
Do you believe something internally bad or uncomfortable would happen if you stopped doing these repetitive checks?

I think… yes, but it’s hard to explain without making it sound bigger than it is.

If I stop before it feels right, I get this really uncomfortable unsettled feeling, like I’ve left something wrong or careless. So I’ll end up rereading the label text, nudging the same objects on the table, and checking the layout photos again and again until it feels more “settled.” Part of me does know it’s already fine, honestly, and I’m probably just losing studio time… but in the moment it feels really hard to leave it alone. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt are significantly interfering with your daily life and causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, because I am still getting most of my work done. It’s not like everything has fallen apart.

But it has started to cost me time in the studio, more than I’d like to admit. I missed a grant deadline because I kept getting stuck on the memorial piece, and I also backed out of a gallery talk I’d actually wanted to do. So… I guess yes, it is interfering, even if part of me wants to say it’s “not that bad.”
Do you feel like these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt are recurring and persistent, even when you try to think about other things?

Yes… they do come back. I wish I could say it was just a normal worry that passed, but when I was working on my aunt’s memorial piece, the same thoughts kept popping up even when I tried to focus on something else.

It would be like, “If I put this photo in the wrong place, or choose the wrong color, does that mean I’m dishonoring her?” Or worse, “Does that mean I didn’t love her enough?” I know that sounds dramatic, and I don’t really believe it in a clear, logical way, but the thoughts felt intrusive and hard to shake. I couldn’t just treat them like ordinary creative doubts.

But with my aunt’s memorial piece, I kept having these really awful, unwanted thoughts that if I chose wrong, it meant I was dishonoring her somehow… or that I didn’t love her enough. I feel embarrassed saying that, because I do know it doesn’t sound fully rational. But I couldn’t just brush it off like normal creative doubt.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's repetitive behaviors are driven by a fear of the consequences of not performing them
doctor.question: Do you believe something internally bad or uncomfortable would happen if you stopped doing these repetitive checks?

target_item.name: Compulsions
target_item.manifestation: I’ll end up rereading the label text, nudging the same objects on the table, and checking the layout photos over and over until it feels ‘settled,’ even though part of me knows it’s already fine and I’m just losing studio time.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the purpose of the repetitive checking and whether stopping it would lead to internal discomfort or distress, which directly relates to compulsions.

patient.answer:
I think… yes, but it’s hard to explain without making it sound bigger than it is.

If I stop before it feels right, I get this really uncomfortable unsettled feeling, like I’ve left something wrong or careless. So I’ll end up rereading the label text, nudging the same objects on the table, and checking the layout photos again and again until it feels more “settled.” Part of me does know it’s already fine, honestly, and I’m probably just losing studio time… but in the moment it feels really hard to leave it alone. Does that answer what you mean?

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's thoughts are intrusive and distressing enough to meet the criteria for obsessive-compulsive disorder
doctor.question: Do you feel like these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt are significantly interfering with your daily life and causing you a lot of distress?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’m still getting most of my work done, but the extra time I lose in the studio already cost me a grant deadline and made me back out of a gallery talk I had actually wanted to do.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the thoughts are causing significant distress and interfering with daily life, which is directly about functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, because I am still getting most of my work done. It’s not like everything has fallen apart.

But it has started to cost me time in the studio, more than I’d like to admit. I missed a grant deadline because I kept getting stuck on the memorial piece, and I also backed out of a gallery talk I’d actually wanted to do. So… I guess yes, it is interfering, even if part of me wants to say it’s “not that bad.”

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thoughts are obsessive in nature
doctor.question: Do you feel like these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt are recurring and persistent, even when you try to think about other things?

target_item.name: Obsessions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because when I was working on my aunt’s memorial piece, I kept getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow—like one wrong photo placement or color choice would mean I didn’t love her enough—and I couldn’t just brush them off like normal creative doubts.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the thoughts about dishonoring her aunt are recurrent, persistent, intrusive, and difficult to suppress, which directly matches obsessions.

patient.answer:
Yes… they do come back. I wish I could say it was just a normal worry that passed, but when I was working on my aunt’s memorial piece, the same thoughts kept popping up even when I tried to focus on something else.

It would be like, “If I put this photo in the wrong place, or choose the wrong color, does that mean I’m dishonoring her?” Or worse, “Does that mean I didn’t love her enough?” I know that sounds dramatic, and I don’t really believe it in a clear, logical way, but the thoughts felt intrusive and hard to shake. I couldn’t just treat them like ordinary creative doubts.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of recurring, intrusive thoughts about dishonoring their aunt, and the compulsive need to perform specific rituals to alleviate anxiety, are characteristic of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).
